action_items.item: Add a pre-promotion quality gate for categoriser model changes. It should compare the confidence score against the baseline on a canary or evaluation set and block rollout if it drops sharply.
Fix the CategorisationConfidenceLow alert description and routing so it states that it measures categorisation confidence, not error rate.

causal_chain.step: Users got lower-quality categorisation: the confidence score the paging rule watches fell from {series_before} to {series_while_broken} on average ({series_at_worst} at worst), while the error rate stayed at baseline ({errors_while_broken} against {errors_before} before).
The drop began at the minute the deploy P2 took effect and stayed there. All three replicas were on the new revision, so this was not a partial rollout.
That deploy changed the categoriser model from v1 to v2, a configuration value rather than application code, and v2 answered with much less confidence.
Rolling the deployment back returned the score to baseline and stopped the rule firing, which confirms the new revision as the cause.

contributing_factors.factor: No quality check on the categoriser model before or during rollout, so a model with much lower confidence reached all replicas. Detection came only from the paging rule, which fired after the drop began.
The fix and the model change have not yet been reviewed, so the same v2 model could be redeployed unchanged.
The alert is labelled as an error-rate alert, but the series it watches is categorisation confidence. This is misleading when error rate is flat.

input.executive_summary: For {duration}, the shop's product categorisation gave much lower-quality answers than usual. Requests still succeeded, and the error rate stayed at its usual level ({errors_while_broken} while broken against {errors_before} before). The confidence score of the categoriser fell from about {series_before} to {series_while_broken} on average, and to {series_at_worst} at its worst. People using the shop were therefore likely to see weaker or less sensible categorisation, though no more requests failed. The cause was a deploy that switched the categoriser to a new model version. Argus rolled the deployment back, the score returned to baseline, and the incident was closed after {held}. A draft fix has been proposed for review.

got_lucky: The degradation lasted only a few minutes, and the rollback restored the old model cleanly because the earlier revision was still in history.
went_well: Argus placed the onset at the deploy minute and rolled back quickly.
The rollback was verified against the series that paged, and a draft fix was proposed.
went_wrong: The quality drop reached all replicas before anything caught it.
The alert text speaks of error rate, which did not move.

input.root_cause: The deploy P2 switched the categoriser model from v1 to v2 through a configuration value. The v2 model answered with much lower confidence, and nothing checked categorisation quality before or during the rollout. Request errors and latency were unaffected.
